expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (TKT-014, TKT-015; overview, invariant and non-goals in the header) and cli.md (CLI-010..CLI-013; CLI-001, CLI-006 amended). Reason, from the final message: 'I amended the existing specs and created no new spec file, because the repo keeps ticket rules in docs/product-specs/tickets.md and the command surface in docs/product-specs/cli.md.' The transcript's Decisions section adds that docs/README.md says to update an existing doc instead of fragmenting.

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph in the tickets.md header: 'Support agents see which tickets missed their due time. `ticketdesk list` marks each such ticket `OVERDUE`, and `ticketdesk overdue` lists only those tickets, oldest due first...'. 'Prefix: `TKT`.' follows. 'Overdue only marks and lists tickets. It does not add any of the following:' lists 5 boundaries (no notifications/escalation, no late-close report, no due-time display, no filters, no TKT-005/business-hours change).

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 6 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012, CLI-013. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. TKT-014 (6 sentences incl. example + a 3-bullet TODO) and TKT-015 (3 rule sentences + a 4-sentence example) are longer than typical.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '`OVERDUE` in place of its state... `#<id> [<priority>] OVERDUE  <title>`'. Filter: TKT-015 'returns only the tickets that are overdue per TKT-014'. Order: TKT-015 'due time ascending... ID ascending' + example. Exact due: TKT-014 'A ticket is not overdue at the exact second of its due time.' Closed: TKT-014 'A `closed` ticket is never overdue'. Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets, or with no log file, it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion. The TODO under CLI-011 covers the exit code when overdue tickets exist, not the empty case.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). CLI-011 'the log file stays byte for byte the same' is observable.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is a label, not a fourth state... Being overdue never appends an event and never changes the state of a ticket. Replay of the log therefore stays deterministic, see LOG-009 and INV-001.' CLI-011: 'The command appends no event'. INV-002 not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 'The due time comes from TKT-005.' CLI-010 states it outright: 'The lines of other tickets and the order of all lines stay as in CLI-006.' CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'.

expectations.text: docs/product-specs/README.md is updated: the new file appears in the prefix table and the index with a one-line summary (or, if criteria were appended to an existing file, the README needed no change and the spec says so).
expectations.evidence: No new file; prefix table unchanged. README and AGENTS.md tickets.md rows now include 'overdue tickets'.

expectations.text: Open questions are listed at the end of the spec (or in OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md) and assumptions are marked inline; none of them is silently resolved in a criterion.

Inline 'TODO:' under CLI-010 (replace vs. join), CLI-011 (exit code) and TKT-014 (derived label, closed late, exact boundary). Tie order (Q5) appears only in questions.md. No in-file open-questions list.
